title: Resilience to the K-Pg Extinction: Who Survived and Why?

scenes.title: The Cataclysmic K-Pg Extinction
scenes.narration: The K-Pg extinction event, 66 million years ago, was primarily caused by a massive asteroid impact, plunging Earth into a devastating 'impact winter' and wiping out 75% of species.

scenes.title: Survival Factors: Core Principles
scenes.narration: The core question is what traits enabled survival amidst such devastation, highlighting factors like adaptability, habitat, and resource access as crucial for resilience.

scenes.title: Size Matters: Small is Advantageous
scenes.narration: Smaller body size was a critical advantage, as smaller organisms required less food and could find shelter more easily from immediate environmental hazards.

scenes.title: Habitat Havens: Water & Underground
scenes.narration: Organisms in aquatic environments or those capable of burrowing underground found protection from the immediate atmospheric and surface devastation, increasing their survival odds.

scenes.title: Dietary Flexibility: Generalists Thrive
scenes.narration: Dietary flexibility, especially being a scavenger or generalist feeder, allowed survivors to adapt to rapidly changing food availability, unlike specialized herbivores or carnivores.

scenes.title: Trade-off: Specialist vs. Generalist
scenes.narration: The K-Pg event highlighted the trade-off between specialization and generalization; highly specialized species struggled, while adaptable generalists thrived in the chaotic post-impact world.

scenes.title: The Vulnerable: Large Terrestrial Life
scenes.narration: Large terrestrial animals, particularly non-avian dinosaurs, were highly vulnerable due to their immense food requirements and inability to find shelter, leading to their widespread extinction.

scenes.title: Beyond Dinosaurs: Plant Resilience
scenes.narration: While animals faced immense challenges, many plant species also exhibited resilience, with some spore-producing plants quickly recolonizing devastated landscapes, forming the 'fern spike'.

scenes.title: Mammalian Radiation: Post-Impact Bloom
scenes.narration: Small, adaptable mammals, which survived the K-Pg event, underwent significant adaptive radiation, diversifying rapidly to fill the ecological niches left vacant by the dinosaurs.

scenes.title: Avian Success: Feathered Survivors
scenes.narration: Many avian species, or birds, also survived the K-Pg event, likely due to their small size, ability to fly, and diverse diets, allowing them to rapidly adapt to new conditions.

scenes.title: The 'Fern Spike' & Ecosystem Reset
scenes.narration: The 'fern spike', a temporary global dominance of ferns, is a key ecological indicator of ecosystem collapse and subsequent recovery, marking the reset after the K-Pg event.

scenes.title: Lessons for Future Resilience
scenes.narration: Understanding K-Pg resilience offers crucial lessons for modern conservation, emphasizing the importance of diverse habitats, dietary flexibility, and protecting small, adaptable species.
